title: Joy
hook: the joy of the Lord is your strength
tomorrow: why is a line from a prison letter printed on gym shirts?

segments.voice: Yesterday one man in ten turned back, and Jesus called him this stranger. The line: everything is gift. Now a crowd that can't stop crying.
screen: `EVERYTHING IS GIFT.` → `NOW, A CROWD IN TEARS.`

segments.voice: A funeral lunch, and somebody tells the story about Grandpa and the lawn mower, and the whole room laughs through its tears. Can you feast on the same day you cried? One crowd in the Bible was told to, and that's the odd part. They stand in the street before the water gate in Jerusalem while Ezra the scribe reads the book of the law aloud, from morning until midday. And they weep. Then their leaders stop them. Not with a sermon on sorrow. With an order to throw a party.
screen: `LAUGHING THROUGH TEARS.` → `THE CROWD WEEPS AT THE WORDS.` → `THE ORDER: FEAST.`

segments.voice: Here's the order, from Nehemiah: “Go your way, eat the fat, and drink the sweet, and send portions unto them for whom nothing is prepared: for this day is holy unto our Lord: neither be ye sorry; for the joy of the LORD is your strength.” So why stop the tears? The text gives the reason: the day is holy, a feast day. Weeping has its place. Ecclesiastes says there is “A time to weep, and a time to laugh.” This was the time to laugh. Notice what's built into the party: portions sent to anyone with nothing ready. Joy here isn't private; nobody is left out of it. Then the strange phrase itself: the joy of the LORD. Readers take it two ways. Joy in the LORD, the gladness people find in God. Or the LORD's own joy, shared with his people. Either way, the crowd doesn't have to manufacture it. It's given, and it holds them up. And here's the turn worth telling a friend: the chapter says they went off “to make great mirth, because they had understood the words that were declared unto them.” The same words that made them cry became the reason to feast. Some Christians put it this way: happiness rises and falls with what happens; joy can sit underneath it, the way a floor sits under a room.
screen: `WHY STOP THE TEARS? A HOLY DAY.` · `A TIME TO LAUGH.` · `SEND PORTIONS: NOBODY LEFT OUT.` · `THE WORDS THAT MADE THEM CRY.` · then, large: `JOY IS STRENGTH.`

segments.voice: Pick one simple good thing within reach: a sip of something warm, a bite of something sweet. Taste it slowly, as if it were the feast, with no phone and no next thing. If you pray, let the enjoying itself be the thanks.
Joy. A gladness that is given, not manufactured, and that holds people up, even on a day that began in tears.
Pocket this one: joy is strength; the crowd in tears went home to feast and share. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Christians mark joy in worship through singing, shared meals and feast days; some read Nehemiah 8:10 as a reminder that joy in God can hold steady even in hard seasons.

match.prompt: the day of tears and the feast — tap the pairs.

fork.setup: your team loses the final. the coach still takes everyone for pizza, and makes sure the bench kid who never got in gets the first slice. which part of Nehemiah 8 is that?
options: send portions to them for whom nothing is prepared.
neither be ye sorry: act like the loss never happened.
read the law aloud from morning until midday.
fork.reveal: the feast had a rule built in: send portions to anyone with nothing ready. joy shared, so nobody is left out.

original.note: Hebrew: joy, gladness. the word in 'the joy of the LORD is your strength' (Nehemiah 8:10).

trapdoor: what you thought: joy is a happy mood that comes and goes.
what it means: a gladness given by God that holds people up.
what a scholar hears: 'the joy of the LORD' can mean joy in God, or God's own joy, shared; and the feast it powers sends food to people with nothing ready.
guess: a deep gladness, given, that holds you up
a cheerful mood you keep up for others
the feeling of finally getting what you want

chat.says: pop wants a cookout saturday, 'before they cut me open.' dad thinks partying before surgery is weird
options: Not weird. Nehemiah sent a crying crowd to feast. Joy can be strength going in.
Kind of. Joy should wait until the surgery's over and he's safe.
Only if everyone hides how scared they are. That's what joy is.
chat.meaning: Nehemiah tells a weeping crowd to feast because the day is holy: the joy of the LORD is your strength. Joy holds people up before the hard part, too.

Ezra.meaning: a priest and scribe who read the law to the people

Nehemiah.meaning: a leader in Jerusalem who stood with Ezra that day

scribe.meaning: someone trained to copy, read and teach the scriptures

mirth.meaning: an old word for merriment and laughter

Ecclesiastes.meaning: a wisdom book of the Hebrew Bible
